'''Carol Lynn Curchoe''' (born in 1979 in [[Manchester, Connecticut]]), formerly Carol George, is an American reproductive biologist specializing in [[Molecular biology]], [[Cell biology]] and [[Biotechnology]]. Her key contributions to those fields include advances in stem cell culture, epigenetics and reprogramming. She is the former [https://web.archive.org/web/20131215002040/http://business.utah.gov/publications/state-science-advisor-2/ Utah State Science Advisor],<ref name="2013 Annual Report">{{cite web|title=Utah Governor's Office of Economic Development 2013 Annual Report|url=http://business.utah.gov/publications/state-science-advisor-2/|website=Business.Utah.gov|publisher=Utah Governor's Office of Economic Development|access-date=1 February 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170405170900/http://business.utah.gov/publications/state-science-advisor-2/|archive-date=5 April 2017}}</ref> President and CEO of [https://www.32atps.com/ 32ATPs],<ref name="32ATPs">{{cite web|title=32ATPs|url=http://www.32atps.com/|website=32ATPs|access-date=1 February 2017}}</ref> domestic outreach director of We Love GMO's and Vaccines<ref>{{cite web|title=About Us|url=http://welovegv.com/about/|website=We Love GMO's and Vaccines|access-date=1 February 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170213025836/http://welovegv.com/about/|archive-date=13 February 2017}}</ref> and an author of personal essays and fiction.

==Career==

===Academics===
Curchoe earned an Associate of Science degree at [[Manchester Community College (Connecticut)|Manchester Community College]], a bachelor's degree, master's degree, and Ph.D. at the [[University of Connecticut]]<ref name="Mentoring">{{cite journal|last1=Curchoe|first1=Carol|title=The Power of Mentoring|journal=Science|volume=350|issue=6259|page=478|bibcode=2015Sci...350..478C|year=2015|doi=10.1126/science.350.6259.478|pmid=26494760|doi-access=free}}</ref> and performed her postdoctoral research at [[Sanford Burnham Prebys Medical Discovery Institute]] as a [[California Institute for Regenerative Medicine]] funded postdoctoral scholar.<ref>{{cite web|title=Carol Lynn Curchoe Is A STEM Warrior Princess|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/christinawallace/2017/01/23/the-limit-does-not-exist-stem-warrior-princess/#45b2953b5c57|website=The Limit Does Not Exist|publisher=Forbes|access-date=4 April 2017|archive-date=5 April 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170405172722/https://www.forbes.com/sites/christinawallace/2017/01/23/the-limit-does-not-exist-stem-warrior-princess/#45b2953b5c57}}</ref>

Her [[California Institute for Regenerative Medicine]] postdoctoral work was performed at the [[Sanford Burnham Prebys Medical Discovery Institute]] in the field of human [[embryonic stem cell]] culture where she developed a protocol for the production of hESC derived neural precursors<ref>{{cite journal |doi=10.1002/stem.107 |title=Nicotinamide Rescues Human Embryonic Stem Cell-Derived Neuroectoderm from Parthanatic Cell Death |year=2009 |last1=Cimadamore |first1=Flavio |last2=Curchoe |first2=Carol Lynn |last3=Alderson |first3=Nazilla |last4=Scott |first4=Fiona |last5=Salvesen |first5=Guy |last6=Terskikh |first6=Alexey V. |journal=Stem Cells |volume=27 |issue=8 |pages=1772–81 |pmid=19544437 |pmc=4151857}}</ref> and peripheral neurons,<ref>{{cite journal |doi=10.1371/journal.pone.0013890 |title=Early Acquisition of Neural Crest Competence During hESCs Neuralization |year=2010 |editor1-last=Najbauer |editor1-first=Joseph |last1=Curchoe |first1=Carol Lynn |last2=Maurer |first2=Jochen |last3=McKeown |first3=Sonja J. |last4=Cattarossi |first4=Giulio |last5=Cimadamore |first5=Flavio |last6=Nilbratt |first6=Mats |last7=Snyder |first7=Evan Y. |last8=Bronner-Fraser |first8=Marianne |last9=Terskikh |first9=Alexey V. |journal=PLOS ONE |volume=5 |issue=11 |article-number=e13890 |pmid=21085480 |pmc=2976694|bibcode=2010PLoSO...513890C |doi-access=free }}</ref> specifically for therapeutic use. Additionally, she developed an in vitro model of early human neurulation events.<ref>{{cite journal |doi=10.1016/j.scr.2011.11.003 |title=HESC derived neuro-epithelial rosettes recapitulate early mammalian neurulation events; an in vitro model |year=2012 |last1=Curchoe |first1=Carol Lynn |last2=Russo |first2=Joseph |last3=Terskikh |first3=Alexey V. |journal=Stem Cell Research |volume=8 |issue=2 |pages=239–46 |pmid=22265743|doi-access=free }}</ref>

As a [[Utah Valley University]] [[adjunct professor]] she taught mammalian cloning and biotechnology using project based learning, inverted classrooms, and community building through social media.

===STEM Education Advocacy===
From May 2013 to May 2014, Curchoe was the Utah State Science Advisor<ref name="Mentoring"/> to Governor [[Gary R. Herbert]]. She was responsible for a number of statewide science initiatives, including the [https://stem.utah.gov/ Utah State STEM Action Center],<ref>{{cite web|title=STEM Action Center|url=https://stem.utah.gov/|website=STEM Action Center UTAH|access-date=1 February 2017}}</ref> [[Utah Governor's Medal for Science and Technology]], Work Ready Utah powered by ACT, and other workforce and advanced manufacturing initiatives.

In an article for Science Magazine, Curchoe stated "I have worked to pay it forward by acting as a mentor for girls and women in STEM, passing on the advice that has worked for me".<ref name="Mentoring"/>

===Business career===
After finishing her academic research Curchoe entered into business development as an associate at [[Sanford Burnham Prebys Medical Discovery Institute]] where she was part of a team that strengthened translational research by establishing clinical research partnerships with [[Pfizer]], [[Takeda Pharmaceutical Company|Takeda]], and [[Johnson & Johnson]]. In 2010 she helped to launch the Office of Collaborative Science<ref>{{cite web|title=Office of Collaborative Science|url=http://www.med.nyu.edu/ocs/home|website=Division of Advanced Research Technologies|access-date=1 February 2017}}</ref> at the [[New York University School of Medicine]], which unified 17 disparate fee for service labs. Best practice models for tracking core-contributed publications<ref>{{cite journal |pmid=23204927 | doi=10.7171/jbt.12-2304-003 | volume=23 | issue=4 | title=Method for tracking core-contributed publications | pmc=3468145 | year=2012 | journal=J Biomol Tech | pages=122–7 | last1 = Loomis | first1 = CA | last2 = Curchoe | first2 = CL}}</ref> resulted.

Curchoe founded 32ATPs,<ref name="32ATPs"/> a company developing a biological supercapacitor which received an honorable mention at the 14th Annual [https://www.utahinnovationawards.com/ Utah Innovation Awards] in the category Clean Technology and Energy.<ref>{{cite web|title=Finalists Announced in 14th Annual Utah Innovation Awards|url=https://www.utahinnovationawards.com/blog/2016/03/29/finalists-announced-in-14th-annual-utah-innovation-awards/|website=Utah Innovation Awards|publisher=Utah Technology Council|access-date=14 March 2017}}</ref> The project was initially crowd-sourced.<ref>{{cite web|title=Can our cell's mitochondria power a cell phone?|url=https://experiment.com/projects/can-our-cell-s-mitochondria-power-a-cell-phone|website=experiment|access-date=13 March 2017}}</ref> The company has applied for a patent for this technology.<ref>{{cite web|title=Biological supercapacitor structure and method for manufacturing and use of the same|url=http://appft.uspto.gov/netacgi/nph-Parser?Sect1=PTO2&Sect2=HITOFF&p=1&u=%2Fnetahtml%2FPTO%2Fsearch-bool.html&r=1&f=G&l=50&co1=AND&d=PG01&s1=curchoe.IN.&OS=IN/curchoe&RS=IN/curchoe|website=Patent Application Full Text and Image Database|publisher=US Patent & Trademark Office|access-date=15 March 2017}}</ref>

Curchoe is known to actively mentor women researchers, staff members and students who are just getting interested in a career in science. She credits the mentorship she received working in the laboratory of Dr. X. Cindy Tian for being able to earn a graduate degree after dropping out of high school.<ref name="Mentoring"/> Since relocating to Utah she has been involved with community initiatives such as [[Latinos in Action]], [[Expanding Your Horizons]]<ref>[http://www.eyhn.org/ Expanding Your Horizons]</ref> and [[Salt Lake Valley Science and Engineering Fair]].<ref>[https://slvsef.org/ Salt Lake Valley Science and Engineering Fair]</ref>

Along with CJ Burton, Curchoe is co-founder of [https://web.archive.org/web/20170405171250/https://www.edupaperproducts.com/ EduPaper Products],<ref>{{cite web|title=EduPaper Products|url=https://www.edupaperproducts.com/|website=EduPaper Products|access-date=13 March 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170405171250/https://www.edupaperproducts.com/|archive-date=5 April 2017}}</ref> an online store selling STEM-themed educational products.
